propositions: Compaction writes SNAPSHOT.json and *.retired files non-atomically in a detached sweep without rollback on worker death, leaving the working tree dirty with untracked files.
When reconverge runs git merge origin/tickets after a peer pushes the same *.retired/SNAPSHOT paths to origin, the merge fails with 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge' abort.

The current merge abort handler is abort-only and push-recovery cannot clear untracked files (git reset --hard is tracked-only, stash -u omitted), causing every retry to re-abort and permanently wedging the store.
Local ticket events become stranded off origin when the merge wedges, with no automatic recovery path.

The fix detects the untracked-overwrite abort in _union_merge, parses the exact paths git names, relocates them to a git-common-dir quarantine directory, and retries the merge once to keep both parents and restore convergence.
After fix, genuine content conflicts still abort and keep local behavior unchanged, while untracked files not named by git and .tmp-event-* at tracker root are never quarantined.
